name: Star Nav
subtitle: Live star map & sky guide
promotionalText: Point your phone at the sky and see the stars, planets and constellations that are really there. Fully offline, no account, no ads.
description:
Star Nav is a real-time map of the night sky. Hold your phone up and the map follows where you point it, labelling the stars, constellations, planets and deep-sky objects in that part of the sky.

SEE WHAT'S UP THERE
• More than 3,000 stars, 88 constellations and 135 galaxies, nebulae and clusters
• The Sun, the Moon and the planets in their true positions, with the Moon's real phase
• Meteor showers shown while they are active
• RA/Dec and alt/az grids, the horizon and the ecliptic, each easy to switch on or off

FIND ANYTHING
• Search by name or catalog designation: "Andromeda", "M31", "Vega"
• Follow the arrow to your target, or let the map glide to it
• Tap any object for a photo, a description, fun facts and when it next rises and sets

EXPLORE TIME
• Travel to any date from 1800 to 2049 and watch the sky move
• Jump to the next sunset, sunrise, moonrise, full moon or new moon

MADE FOR NIGHT USE
• Night mode turns everything red to protect your dark-adapted eyes
• Works entirely offline: no account, no ads, no tracking

Star Nav is free, open-source software (GPLv3), built on an open-source Android planetarium. Imagery courtesy of NASA, ESA, ESO, the IAU and others, credited in the app.
reviewNotes:
Star Nav is an offline planetarium. No login is required and there is no in-app purchase.

• Point the device at the sky (or anywhere): the star map follows the device orientation using the motion sensors. Tap the hand/compass button (bottom right) to switch to manual mode, then drag to pan and pinch to zoom.
• Location permission is optional; if denied, the app uses a default location, and one can be entered under ⋯ → Settings.
• Try: Search (magnifier) → "Moon" or "M31"; tap any labelled object for its info card; Time Travel (clock icon) → "Full Moon".
• All content is bundled; the app makes no network requests of its own.
• The app is free software (GPLv3, source at https://github.com/stasgold/Sky-Map). It is an independent iOS port of an open-source Android planetarium and uses its own name and artwork; third-party imagery is credited under ⋯ → About & Credits.
